name: Algaz Station
summary: At Algaz Station, Mountaineers guard the northern road from Loch Modan toward the Wetlands. The outpost lies south of Dun Algaz, where the pass leads through the mountains.

sections.title: Watching the Northern Pass
sections.body: At Algaz Station, dwarven Mountaineers watch the road north from Loch Modan. The post lies east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, guarding the route between the kingdom of Ironforge and the northern lowlands. The road carries trade and troops through the mountain tunnels, but the hills bring danger from wandering beasts and troggs. Mountaineers keep the way open and offer weary travelers a place for respite, repairs, and martial support before they enter the pass.

faq.answer: Algaz Station is an Ironforge military outpost in northwestern Loch Modan. Mountaineers guard the mountain passes leading north to Dun Algaz and aid travelers on the way.

faq.q: Where does the station get its name?
aliases: why is it called algaz station
faq.answer: The station takes its name from Dun Algaz, the massive dwarven pass and tunnel system just to its north. It connects Loch Modan to the Wetlands.

faq.q: Who can be found at Algaz Station?
faq.answer: Dwarven Mountaineers man the outpost, including Mountaineer Stormpike. Armorer Gothor Brumn provides field repairs to travelers.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you know Algaz Station as a sign of Ironforge's reach. Its Mountaineers guard the king's highways against threats from the mountains.
As an Alliance traveler, you can use the outpost as a secure staging ground and repair stop on the way between Loch Modan and the northern marshlands.
